about: Bundled examples, in menu order. Each file is the RCSB PDB mmCIF (anisotropic displacement parameters removed to save space) or an AlphaFold DB model, gzipped. "view" lists the commands that set up the opening view when the example is chosen from the menu.

examples.label: EGFR kinase with erlotinib
examples.description: Erlotinib (Tarceva), a lung-cancer drug, in the ATP site of the EGFR kinase domain. Opens on the binding site with its hydrogen bonds and contacts.
examples.credit: Stamos et al., J Biol Chem 2002

examples.label: ABL kinase with imatinib
examples.description: Imatinib (Gleevec) bound to the inactive, DFG-out ABL kinase: the drug that made chronic myeloid leukemia a manageable disease.
examples.credit: Cowan-Jacob et al., Acta Cryst D 2007

examples.label: BRAF V600E with vemurafenib
examples.description: Vemurafenib (PLX4032) in the kinase domain of BRAF V600E, the driver mutation of half of all melanomas. The drug occupies chain A; the mutant Glu600 is modeled in chain B.

examples.label: KRAS G12C with sotorasib
examples.description: Sotorasib (AMG 510), the first approved KRAS drug, bonded covalently to Cys12 of KRAS G12C next to GDP and Mg²⁺.

examples.label: PI3Kα H1047R with alpelisib
examples.description: Cryo-EM structure of the oncogenic PI3Kα H1047R mutant with its regulatory subunit p85α and alpelisib (BYL-719), a breast-cancer drug.

examples.label: IDH1 R132H with vorasidenib
examples.description: Mutant IDH1 R132H, which makes the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, with NADPH and vorasidenib (approved for glioma in 2024) in the allosteric pocket at the dimer interface.
examples.credit: Konteatis et al., ACS Med Chem Lett 2020

examples.label: PARP1 with olaparib
examples.description: Olaparib (Lynparza), a PARP inhibitor for BRCA-mutated cancers, in the nicotinamide pocket of the PARP1 catalytic domain.
examples.credit: Ryan et al., J Biol Chem 2021

examples.label: μ-opioid receptor with fentanyl
examples.description: Cryo-EM structure of fentanyl in the μ-opioid receptor, a G protein-coupled receptor, coupled to the Gi heterotrimer (with scFv16 used to stabilize it).

examples.label: PROTAC MZ1 bridging BRD4 and VHL
examples.description: The PROTAC MZ1 joins the second bromodomain of BRD4 to the VHL E3 ligase. The new protein–protein contacts it induces explain its selectivity for BRD4.
examples.credit: Gadd et al., Nat Chem Biol 2017

examples.label: Lenalidomide gluing CK1α to cereblon
examples.description: The molecular glue lenalidomide binds cereblon (with DDB1) and creates a surface that recruits casein kinase 1α for degradation, the basis of its activity in del(5q) myelodysplastic syndrome.

examples.label: PD-1 with PD-L1
examples.description: The immune checkpoint receptor PD-1 bound to its ligand PD-L1, the interaction that checkpoint immunotherapies block.

examples.label: Atezolizumab Fab with PD-L1
examples.description: The therapeutic antibody atezolizumab bound to PD-L1. Add 4ZQK and superpose PD-L1 to see the Fab cover the PD-1 binding site.

examples.label: Trastuzumab Fab with HER2
examples.description: The Fab of trastuzumab (Herceptin) bound to domain IV of the HER2 extracellular region, the target in HER2-positive breast cancer.

examples.label: T-cell receptor with a KRAS G12D neoantigen
examples.description: A high-affinity T-cell receptor recognizing the KRAS G12D peptide VVVGADGVGK presented by HLA-A*11:01.

examples.label: p53 DNA-binding domain on DNA
examples.description: The p53 core domain on its DNA response element. The most frequent cancer mutations (R175, R248, R273) are shown; R248 and R273 contact the DNA directly.

examples.label: MDM2 with the p53 transactivation peptide
examples.description: The p53 transactivation helix in the MDM2 pocket. Phe19, Trp23 and Leu26 are the anchors that MDM2 inhibitors such as nutlins mimic.

examples.label: BRCA1 BRCT repeats with a phosphopeptide
examples.description: The tandem BRCT repeats of BRCA1 recognizing a BACH1 peptide phosphorylated on Ser990 (residue 6 of chain B); cancer mutations here disrupt phosphopeptide binding.

examples.label: Nucleosome with BRCA1–BARD1
examples.description: Cryo-EM structure of the BRCA1–BARD1 RING heterodimer with the E2 enzyme UbcH5c bound to a nucleosome, positioned to ubiquitylate histone H2A.

examples.label: Cas9 with guide RNA and target DNA
examples.description: Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 with its single-guide RNA and target DNA strand; the RNA–DNA heteroduplex sits in a positively charged groove. The crystal holds two complexes; the view shows the first.

examples.label: Adenylate kinase, open and closed
examples.description: Open, substrate-free adenylate kinase (4AKE) with the closed form (1AKE) superposed on the CORE domain of chain A and colored by deviation: the LID and NMP domains swing shut over the substrates.
examples.credit: Müller et al., Structure 1996; Müller & Schulz, J Mol Biol 1992

examples.label: Adenylate kinase with Ap5A (closed)
examples.description: The closed state of adenylate kinase trapping the bisubstrate inhibitor Ap5A between its LID and NMP domains.

examples.label: Hemoglobin, deoxy and oxy
examples.description: Deoxyhemoglobin (T state, 4HHB) with oxyhemoglobin (R state, the 1HHO tetramer) superposed on one αβ dimer: the other dimer shows the quaternary rotation of the T→R transition.
examples.credit: Fermi et al., J Mol Biol 1984; Shaanan, J Mol Biol 1983

examples.label: Oxyhemoglobin
examples.description: Oxyhemoglobin with O₂ bound to each heme. The crystal holds one αβ dimer; the view builds the biological tetramer (assembly 1).

examples.label: BRCA1–BARD1 RING domains (NMR ensemble)
examples.description: Twenty NMR models of the BRCA1–BARD1 RING heterodimer, overlaid and colored by RMSF: the zinc-binding cores are well defined and the termini are flexible.
examples.credit: Brzovic et al., Nat Struct Biol 2001

examples.label: p53, AlphaFold prediction
examples.description: AlphaFold DB model of full-length human p53 with its predicted aligned error: confident DNA-binding and tetramerization domains, disordered termini. Compare it with 1TUP, or find its PAE domains.
examples.credit: AlphaFold DB (Jumper et al., Nature 2021; Varadi et al., Nucleic Acids Res 2024), CC BY 4.0

examples.label: SARS-CoV-2 spike, closed
examples.description: Cryo-EM structure of the prefusion SARS-CoV-2 spike trimer with its N-linked glycans, the antigen of COVID-19 vaccines.

examples.label: AAV2 capsid
examples.description: The adeno-associated virus 2 capsid, a gene-therapy vector. The file holds one VP3 subunit; the view builds the 60-subunit icosahedral shell (assembly 1, 249,000 atoms), each subunit colored N → C.
